Monday: Trisha found a quiz on a video site's community page: "What colour is your soul?" She answered twenty questions in bed. Result: "Deep Blue. You feel things more deeply than others realise, and you are stronger than people think." She read it four times and felt her throat go tight. Finally, someone got it.
Wednesday: She posted the result on her status with the caption "literally me 💙". When Deepika replied, "same, I got Deep Blue too 😅", Trisha typed back, "no, it's different for me, I actually am like this."
Saturday: At lunch her cousins said she was being moody. Trisha held up her phone and read the result aloud as proof. "See? I just feel things more deeply." Later she set the screenshot as her lock screen.

qa.q: What result did Trisha get on the quiz on Monday?
qa.a: "Deep Blue", which said she feels things more deeply than others realise and is stronger than people think.

qa.q: Why did Trisha insist "it's different for me" when Deepika got the same result?
qa.a: The result made her feel truly understood, so admitting it also fits Deepika would take that special feeling away. Her wish to be seen made the vague words feel exact.

qa.q: At the Wednesday moment, what choice could Trisha have made that might have changed how she used the result?
qa.a: When Deepika replied with the same Deep Blue result, Trisha could have paused and asked what that means: if the same words fit both of them, they probably fit most people.

qa.q: How might Trisha's cousins feel when she answers them by reading the quiz aloud?
qa.a: They raised something about her mood and got a quiz result back instead of a real reply, so they may feel brushed aside and find it harder to talk honestly with her.

passage: Arnab, you're showing me your quiz result like it's a medical report! Sit. Your Kalyani Mashi has been there too. When I was fifteen, the cyber café near our Kolkata lane charged by the half hour. I spent a whole week's pocket money on a quiz called "Which Flower Are You?" It said I was a lotus: "Calm on the surface, but full of hidden depth that few people see." I printed it! I carried that page to school and showed every friend, as if it were a certificate of who I was. When anyone called me bossy, I'd say, "No, I'm a lotus, I'm deep." Years later I found my friend Shampa's printout inside an old diary. Hers said lotus too, word for word. I laughed for a whole evening.

qa.q: How did the cyber café near Kalyani's lane charge?
qa.a: It charged by the half hour.

qa.q: Why did young Kalyani carry the printout to school like a certificate?
qa.a: She felt proud and seen, because the lotus result said she had hidden depth few people see, so the printout felt like proof of who she was.

qa.q: What choice could young Kalyani have made when friends called her bossy?
qa.a: Instead of answering with the lotus result, she could have listened to what her friends meant and thought about it. The flattering quiz line was helping her shut out real feedback.

qa.q: Why might Kalyani Mashi be telling this story to Arnab now?
qa.a: Arnab is treating a quiz result like a medical report, and Mashi seems to want Arnab to see, gently and through her own old mistake, how general words can feel personal.

grounding: An aunt recalls how, as a teenager, a flattering and general online quiz result felt like being seen and became her proof of who she was.

passage: The power had gone out in Hrithik's building an hour before his chemistry test, and his phone was at nine percent. He should have been revising by candlelight. People underestimate you, but you have big plans." Hrithik sat up. That was it, exactly. His father always said he lacked direction. He spent a chunk of his last battery forwarding it to Pankaj with "THIS. Show this to anyone who says I'm lazy." Pankaj replied, "mine said the same lol." The phone died before Hrithik could answer. He stared at the black screen, still sure it meant him.

qa.q: What did Hrithik want the quiz result to prove?
qa.a: He wanted proof that he isn't lazy or aimless, since his father said he lacked direction. Being called a misunderstood leader felt like finally being seen. 🥺

qa.q: What choice could Hrithik make after Pankaj said the result was the same?
qa.a: He could take that as a clue that the words are general and fit many people, then close the quiz and use the candlelight for the chemistry test.

qa.a: Pankaj got the same result and treats it lightly with "lol", so to Pankaj it looks like a fun, general quiz rather than a verdict on anyone's character.

'Didi, look. Which Season Are You. I got Autumn.'

'Thoughtful, loyal, and quietly misunderstood by people around you.'

'It's so me. That's literally me.'
'Loyal, okay. Quietly misunderstood?'

'Beta, your dal is getting cold,' said Ma.
'Ma, listen. It says I'm thoughtful. You always say I'm careless.'
'You left the gas on yesterday.'
'That was once! See, misunderstood.'
Urmila took his phone and scrolled. 'What does Spring say?'
'Who cares about Spring.'
'Kind, loyal, and often misunderstood by those close to you.'
'That's different.'
'How?'
Sumit took the phone back. 'Just is.' He changed his profile picture to an orange leaf before finishing his dal.

qa.a: Sumit got Autumn.

qa.q: Why was Sumit so sure the Autumn result was 'literally me'?
qa.a: He wanted to feel understood at home, so 'quietly misunderstood' matched how he felt and made the general words seem exact.

qa.q: What turning point could Sumit have used when Urmila read out Spring?
qa.a: He could have noticed that Spring also said loyal and misunderstood, and asked himself whether the quiz really knew him, instead of saying 'Just is'.

qa.q: How might Urmila Didi see Sumit's reaction to the quiz?
qa.a: Urmila probably sees her brother wanting to be understood, and gently tries to show him the words fit almost anyone.
